title_en: Global X’s Dorson on Active’s Edge in EM Markets
title_zh: Global X的Dorson谈主动管理在新兴市场的优势
subtitle_zh: Global X新兴市场策略主管Malcolm Dorson与彭博行业研究的David Cohne、Sharun Francis探讨：为何高度分散、低效的新兴市场为主动管理创造增值空间，以及投资者如何在宽基指数与更具针对性的国家/地区敞口之间做选择。
summary_zh: 本期 Inside Active 由 Bloomberg Intelligence 的 David Cohne 与联合主持 Sharun Francis 对话 Global X 新兴市场策略主管兼高级投资组合经理 Malcolm Dorson，核心命题是高度分散（dispersion）、低效的新兴市场为何天然适合主动管理。Dorson 强调新兴市场不是单一资产类别，而是一份由不同经济周期、政治环境与货币走势构成的“菜单”，印度的结构性故事与巴西、哥伦比亚可能毫不相干。他把美元视为最重要的驱动变量：历史上美元每走弱 1%，新兴市场股票约上涨略高于 3%；2001 至 2011 年新兴市场累涨近 345%，而 S&P 500 仅约 15%。他的配置论据是普通顾问仅配约 3% 至 4%，而 MSCI All Country World Index 的基准权重接近 15%，再叠加约 42% 的相对估值折价与趋于收敛的 EPS 增速。主动优势他归为三点：宽基指数的集中度风险；国有或创始家族控股下少数股东利益不一致，如关联交易、股权质押与盘根错节的集团结构，而指数无法追问这些；以及贴近本地的研究能力，其印度策略在孟买有 14 名驻地分析师。他还用 GDP 构成筛选国家，认为印度几项全中，并看好阿根廷、越南与哥伦比亚。结尾他指出主动型新兴市场 ETF 的普及路径是业绩先行、资金先涌入被动，待配置者建立信念、完成尽调后主动管理才真正接管。
description: Global X’s Dorson on Active’s Edge in EM Markets

turns.en: Welcome to Inside Active, a podcast about active managers that goes beyond soundbites and headlines and looks deeper into their processes, challenges, and philosophies in security selection. I'm David Cohn. I lead mutual fund and active research at Bloomberg Intelligence. Today, my co-host is Sharun Francis, Associate Analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence. Sharun, thank you for joining me today.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听《Inside Active》，这是一档关于主动管理型基金经理的播客，我们不满足于只言片语和头条标题，而是更深入地探讨他们在选股方面的流程、挑战和理念。我是David Cohne，在彭博行业研究（Bloomberg Intelligence）负责共同基金和主动管理研究。今天与我共同主持的是彭博行业研究的助理分析师Sharun Francis。Sharun，感谢你今天加入。

turns.en: Thanks for having me, David.
turns.zh: 谢谢你邀请我，David。

turns.en: So emerging markets are often grouped together as a single asset class, but with, you know, the countries and companies within them can actually look pretty different. So You know, economic growth, market structure, governance and political risk can vary widely from one market to the next. Those differences can also create challenges for broad emerging market benchmarks, which may be heavily influenced by particular countries, sectors or companies. And that raises an important question for investors. Where can active management add value? And when, you know, might more targeted exposure make sense? And so today I wanted to explore the case for active management in emerging markets. how the opportunity set is evolving, and what investors should consider when choosing between broad and more targeted exposure. Joining me to discuss that is Malcolm Dorsen, a Senior Portfolio Manager for Emerging Market Equities and Head of Emerging Market Strategy at Global X Management Company. Malcolm, thanks for joining us.
turns.zh: 新兴市场常常被归为单一资产类别，但其中的国家和公司实际上可能差异很大。经济增长、市场结构、治理和政治风险在不同的市场之间可能千差万别。这些差异也会给宽基新兴市场基准带来挑战，因为这些基准可能受到特定国家、行业或公司的强烈影响。这就给投资者提出了一个重要问题：主动管理在哪些方面能够创造价值？在什么时候，更有针对性的敞口才是合理的？所以今天我想探讨在新兴市场进行主动管理的理由、机会集是如何演变的，以及投资者在宽基敞口和更有针对性的敞口之间做选择时应考虑什么。今天加入我们讨论的是Global X Management Company的新兴市场股票高级投资组合经理兼新兴市场策略主管Malcolm Dorson。Malcolm，感谢你加入我们。

turns.en: David Schroon, thank you so much for having me.
turns.zh: David、Sharun，非常感谢你们邀请我。

turns.en: So, what do you think defines emerging markets as an investment opportunity today?
turns.zh: 那么，你认为是什么定义了当今新兴市场作为一种投资机会的特质？

turns.en: Yeah, I mean, I think a lot has to do with your introduction, David. Normally, people say a definition of emerging markets, they think about it how MSCI or FTSE might define it in terms of liquidity and access and size. But what do you think about what do you get out of this asset class? It's so much and so diverse. And I think dispersion is the key word. We're looking at different economic cycles, different political environments, various different currencies that behave in different ways and really different drivers of growth. So it works more like a menu than one asset class. And, you know, sometimes a structural story like a country such as India really has nothing to do with something like a country like Brazil or Colombia. So I think it's finding different opportunities and different drivers of growth.
turns.zh: 是的，我觉得这跟你的开场介绍很有关系，David。通常人们给新兴市场下定义时，会想到MSCI或富时（FTSE）如何从流动性、可及性和规模来定义它。但你会从这个资产类别中得到什么呢？它内容极其丰富、极其多元。我认为“分散差异”（dispersion）是关键词。我们面对的是不同的经济周期、不同的政治环境、表现各异的各种货币，以及真正不同的增长驱动因素。所以它更像一份菜单，而不是单一资产类别。有时候，像印度这样一个国家的结构性故事，其实跟巴西或哥伦比亚这样的国家毫无关系。所以我认为关键在于发现不同的机会和不同的增长驱动因素。

turns.en: Malcolm, more broadly speaking, why do you think capital flows have favored U.S. equities for so long? And what could cause that to change over the next few years?
turns.zh: Malcolm，从更宏观的角度来说，你认为为什么资金流长期以来一直青睐美国股票？未来几年又有什么因素可能导致这种情况改变？

turns.en: Well, it's a painful question, Sharun, because I started my career a little over 20 years ago in emerging markets, and it's certainly been the wrong place to be. I think at least over the past 12 to 15 years, we've seen really dramatic outperformance from developed markets and more specifically the S & P. And markets tend to work in cycles. I mean, if you look at period between 2001 and 2011, emerging markets were up close to 345%. while the S & P was just up about 15%. So there is really, throughout history, there have been dramatic periods of both outperformance and underperformance. And the most recent period of outperformance has sort of, for the US, has really compounded upon itself in that people have recency bias, have bias towards what has succeeded, and that's continued to bring in more flows into developed markets. But a big part of it, I have to say, is also the dollar. we're coming out of a very strong U.S. dollar environment over the past 15 years. And that's probably the most important driver of emerging markets as an asset class as a whole. Historically, as the dollar has strengthened or say the dollar weakens 1%, emerging market equities have had a direct inverse relationship by strengthening just over 3%. So that 1 to 3 has been pretty steady and that's kind of kept people away from emerging markets and more towards the U.S. in a strong dollar environment.
turns.zh: 嗯，这是个让人痛苦的问题，Sharun，因为我在20多年前入行时做的就是新兴市场，而这显然一直是个错误的地方。我认为至少在过去12到15年间，我们看到发达市场——更具体地说是标普500指数——出现了非常显著的超额表现。而市场往往以周期方式运行。如果你看看2001年到2011年这段时间，新兴市场上涨了近345%，而标普500只上涨了约15%。所以纵观历史，确实出现过大幅跑赢和大幅跑输的时期。而最近这一轮美国市场的超额表现其实是自我强化的，因为人们有近因偏差，倾向于追捧已经成功的东西，这就持续把更多资金带入发达市场。但我不得不说，其中很大一部分原因还在于美元。过去15年我们正走出一个美元极其强势的环境。这大概是新兴市场作为一个整体资产类别最重要的驱动因素。从历史来看，当美元走强——或者说美元每走弱1%，新兴市场股票都存在一种直接的反向关系，会上涨略高于3%。这种1对3的关系相当稳定，也正是它在强势美元环境下把人们挡在新兴市场之外、更多地推向美国市场。

turns.en: So what do you think, you know, this is kind of a follow-up to that, you know, what do you think has changed about emerging markets over the past decade that investors who just might not have paid attention to, you know, the market might be missing?
turns.zh: 那么，接着这个话题往下问，你认为过去十年里新兴市场发生了哪些变化，是那些可能没太关注市场的投资者会错过的？

turns.en: Well, a lot's changed. I mean, whether it be the size of China, whether it be the emergence and dynamism of the semiconductor industry, whether it be, you know, just political and economic reform in terms of looking at trade balances, looking at fiscal balances. We used to speak about the fragile five and these countries that had fiscal deficits close to 5% of GDP. Now, most of these emerging market countries have deficits less than 3%. You've seen a lot of reform. You see a lot more autonomy in terms of central banks. But in terms of if I'm sitting in the U.S. as an allocator, and I'm way more excited about what has changed over the past 12 months, over the past two years, where I don't think people have been paying attention, is that we're starting to see signs of that cycle changing. So whether it be broad emerging markets or emerging markets, ex-China, really have dramatically outperformed the U.S. over the past couple of years, despite the U.S. actually performing quite well in itself. So people are starting to take a look at that because their position is quite low. The average advisor that we speak with has roughly a 3%, 4% allocation to emerging markets. But if you look at MSCI, All Country World Index, that allocation from a benchmark perspective is closer to 15%. meaning that a lot of people are more than 10 percentage points underweight emerging markets. So it's not necessarily people are saying, I need to sell Apple and buy Alibaba and go all in or overweight on emerging markets. What people are saying is I've done really well and now there's a lot of uncertainty. We were talking about the dollar earlier. Well, in 2025, the dollar weakened around 10%. This year, despite flight to quality moments with two major wars, a lot of uncertainty, central bank governor change, We started out the year pricing in four cuts. Now the swap market says three or four hikes. In a normal year, you'd think the dollar would be ripping a lot, lot stronger. But structural forces have been keeping the dollar at bay. So it's only been about 23% stronger. So I think with that amount of uncertainty and that low amount of positioning, combined with emerging markets trading at a roughly 42% discount to the S & P with converging EPS growth rates, People are doing their homework and saying maybe it's time to step back into this asset class.
turns.zh: 嗯，变化很多。无论是中国的体量，还是半导体行业的崛起和活力，又或者是政治和经济改革——从贸易差额到财政差额来看。我们过去常提到“脆弱五国”（fragile five），那些财政赤字接近GDP 5%的国家。如今，大多数新兴市场国家的赤字都低于3%。你已经看到了大量改革，央行的独立性也大大增强。但如果我是坐在美国的一名资产配置者，更让我兴奋的是过去12个月、过去两年里发生的变化——我认为人们此前没有关注到——那就是我们开始看到周期转变的迹象。无论是宽基新兴市场，还是不含中国的新兴市场，过去几年都大幅跑赢了美国，尽管美国市场本身表现也相当不错。所以人们开始关注这一点，因为他们的仓位非常低。与我们交流的平均一位顾问对新兴市场的配置大约只有3%、4%。但如果你看MSCI全球全国家指数（All Country World Index），从基准角度来看这个配置接近15%，这意味着很多人对新兴市场的低配超过10个百分点。所以并不一定是说人们要卖掉苹果、买入阿里巴巴，全仓押注或超配新兴市场。人们的想法是：我已经赚得相当好了，而现在有太多不确定性。我们刚才谈到美元。嗯，2025年美元贬值了约10%。今年，尽管出现了两场大规模战争带来的避险时刻、大量不确定性、央行行长更替——年初我们还定价四次降息，现在掉期市场却说是三到四次加息。在正常年份，你会以为美元会飙升得非常非常强。但结构性力量一直压制着美元，所以它只强了大约23%。所以我认为，在如此多的不确定性、如此低的仓位配置，再加上新兴市场相对标普500有大约42%的估值折价、每股收益（EPS）增长率又趋于收敛的情况下，人们正在做功课，并在想：也许是时候重新回到这个资产类别了。

turns.en: So I know you mentioned the dollar and things happening here. Just at a high level, I think one of the arguments for emerging markets was always faster economic growth than what you would get here in other developed markets. How does economic growth in emerging markets themselves actually translate into market returns over there?
turns.zh: 我知道你提到了美元和这里发生的事情。仅从宏观层面来说，我认为支持新兴市场的一个论点一直是：相比美国等其他发达市场，那里有更快的经济增长。那么新兴市场自身的经济增长，实际上又是如何转化为当地市场回报的呢？

turns.en: Unfortunately, not as well as you'd hope. It's more of a marketing line. I've always loved to meet with investors and point to the U.S. growing at 2% or 3% and emerging markets growing at 3% to 4%, often really doubling U.S. GDP growth, saying, all right, this is the opportunity. Big discount, but with outsized GDP growth. What's actually really important is getting a valuation discount from a multiple perspective and then pointing that, using that and complementing it with EPS growth and profitability. Because if you have growth and you can't reinvest it in a profitable backdrop, i.e. where your ROEs are higher than your cost of capital, then you're really just looking at a dilutive prospect. But more recently, GDP levels have still been moving in the right direction. We have seen some dollar weakness, but I think most importantly, we're seeing really strong capital allocation decisions coming from the corporates within emerging markets. whether it be sort of the value-up program in Korea, China getting more interested within its capital market system, really pointing out targeted levels of profitability and valuations that they're looking for, whether it be really strong buyback programs that we're seeing in Latin America and countries like Brazil. We're seeing a lot more focus on strong, prudent capital allocation decisions that are aligned with minority shareholders. that are raising levels of profitability and raising levels of EPS growth. And that's when you start getting excited because you have that discount from a multiple perspective, but now all those other variables look good too.
turns.zh: 遗憾的是，转化得并不像你希望的那样好。这更多是一句营销话术。我一直喜欢见投资者时指出：美国增长2%或3%，而新兴市场增长3%到4%，往往是美国GDP增速的两倍，然后说“好吧，这就是机会”——估值大幅折价，但GDP增长超强。真正重要的其实是从估值倍数角度获得折价，然后利用这一折价，并用每股收益（EPS）增长和盈利能力来加以补充。因为如果你有增长，却无法在一个盈利的背景下再投资——也就是说你的净资产收益率（ROE）高于你的资本成本——那么你面对的其实只是一种摊薄的前景。但最近，GDP水平仍然在朝正确方向发展。我们也看到美元有所走弱，但我认为最重要的是，我们看到新兴市场企业内部正在做出非常强劲的资本配置决策。无论是韩国的“企业价值提升计划”（value-up program），中国对其资本市场体系日益重视、明确提出所追求的目标盈利水平和估值，还是我们在拉美和巴西等国家看到的非常强劲的回购计划。我们看到，市场越来越关注那些强劲、审慎、与少数股东利益一致的资本配置决策，它们正在提升盈利水平和每股收益增长水平。而正是这个时候你会开始感到兴奋，因为你不仅从估值倍数角度有了折价，如今其他所有变量看起来也都不错。

turns.en: Circling back to the idea of cycles, if markets do begin to rotate internationally, does that create a greater opportunity for active management to add value? And if it does, what about that environment makes it more favorable?
turns.zh: 回到周期这个话题，如果市场确实开始在国际间轮动，这是否会为主动管理创造更大的增值机会？如果会，那么这种环境的哪些特点使其更有利？

turns.en: Well, I think so because... The way that passive strategies are set up, I think that they'll generally attract that first dollar that comes into emerging markets before investors start saying, or allocators come in and say, all right, this is going to be a long-term investment. I need a good steward of capital. I'm going to do my due diligence. I'm going to interview various managers and really go through a thoughtful process. So when performance starts moving really well, a lot of people come in for it as a trade or to chase momentum. And that's when you get a lot of flows going into passive indexes. And in a lot of these passive indexes, you're in a bunch of... First of all, you have a lot of concentration risk. Second of all, you often are set up in companies that have minimal alignment with minority shareholders. And those valuations tend to suck up the most dollars. Valuations get inflated. And that creates a lot of inefficiencies that active managers can take advantage of.
turns.zh: 嗯，我认为是的，因为……被动策略的构建方式决定了它们通常会吸引流入新兴市场的第一笔资金，然后投资者——或者说配置者——才会开始说：“好吧，这将是一笔长期投资。我需要一个优秀的资本管家。我要做尽职调查，要面谈各家基金管理人，真正走一遍深思熟虑的流程。”所以当业绩开始大幅向好时，很多人是把它当作一笔交易或追逐动量而进场的。而这时就会有大量资金流入被动指数。在很多这类被动指数里，你持有的是一堆……首先，你面临很大的集中度风险。其次，你往往持有的是那些与少数股东利益几乎没有一致性的公司。而这些公司的估值往往吸走了最多的资金，估值被推高。这就造成了大量低效，而主动管理人可以加以利用。

turns.en: On the topic of inefficiencies, when you're thinking about active management in emerging markets, is there one common inefficiency you're trying to capitalize on? Or does that particular inefficiency change given how different these markets can be?
turns.zh: 谈到市场低效这个话题，当你在思考新兴市场的主动管理时，是否有一种共同的市场低效是你试图加以利用的？还是说，鉴于这些市场差异如此之大，那种特定的低效会随之改变？

turns.en: That's a really good question because all of these markets, as we discussed earlier, are quite diverse. But I think that one of the key inefficiencies that I'd be looking for lies around governance. Whether it be a country like in, you know, Brazil, where over 35% of the companies within its market cap are state-owned enterprises, where management teams can change every four years, depending on who wins a federal or local election. And you have government spending for the sake of spending in terms of building a national brand, keep people employed, paying dividends instead of reinvesting into accretive projects. that shows really minimal alignment with minority shareholders. We see something pretty similar in deep markets such as India as well with the promoter culture, but also with state-owned enterprises in India. So across the board, that's something we really try to take advantage of. If you look at emerging markets as a whole, it represents about a quarter of companies by market cap within the index are state-owned enterprises. So we try to stay away from them as a whole unless we find situations where the government kind of has its back against the wall. The balance sheet has been inflated too much. You need a turnaround story. And the government sort of steps aside and says, all right, we're going to institute private management. We are going to allow them to reduce their balance sheet, sell non-core assets, set in really aligned KPIs that make sense for minority shareholders and draw investors back into these types of companies. So sometimes they make some of the best turnaround stories you can find. But as a whole, it's something you have to be really cautious of. And it's probably one of the biggest flaws of the broad indexes. So actually, I got a question to flip that on its head. Is there actually any part of emerging markets where you don't think active management has much of an advantage over indexes? Or is it really active is kind of the best way no matter where you go? No, I think no matter how you do it, I mean, active and passive, I think there are different ways of approaching emerging markets these days. And that's probably one of the biggest differences that we've seen between now and 20 years ago. You used to just come into emerging markets and buy the index and you'd say, okay, this is giving me some diversification. It's giving me some inflation protection, some protection against a potential weaker dollar. But EM has evolved and People haven't looked under the hood as much as they probably should have been over the past few decades. And now you're seeing tremendous concentration risk. You see roughly 40% of the EM index is made up of hardware technology, semiconductors. You see roughly 20% to China, almost 30% to Taiwan, a really significant amount to Korea, and 80% Asia as a whole. So if you take a step back as a casual investor and say, wait a second, I thought I was getting the value trade in Eastern Europe and a structural growth opportunity in Southeast Asia or the political reform story in Latin America. You're really not. You basically get minimal exposure. So from the primary investor, you can do this through passive strategies, but you're being active yourself. So you can say, I actively want to set up my own emerging markets exposure and I can buy passive Argentina, passive Colombia, passive Greece, whatever. passive Vietnam, various countries that have a lot of idiosyncratic, exciting growth drivers that are seeing a lot of momentum right now without buying the broad passive index. Now, the other way, so that's one way of thinking of active, kind of doing it yourself, buying individual country-specific or regional-specific passive countries or passive products, or looking at a, from a broader perspective, saying, I don't have time for that. I can't look at all these countries. I don't know necessarily what's going on. I know I want emerging markets exposure, but I don't like the way the benchmark is set up. Then you go with an active manager who is, you're basically outsourcing your stock picking and country allocation for you. And I think that that's a way that a lot of people prefer to move because you can sort of set and forget it.
turns.zh: 这是个非常好的问题，因为我们前面讨论过，所有这些市场都相当多元。但我认为我会寻找的关键市场低效之一，就存在于治理层面。比如在巴西这样的国家，按市值计算，其市场中有超过35%的公司是国有企业，管理层团队每四年就可能更换一次，取决于谁赢得联邦或地方选举。而且政府为了花钱而花钱——为了打造国家品牌、维持就业、发放股息，而不是再投资于有增值效应的项目，这体现出与少数股东利益几乎没有一致性。在印度这样深度较深的市场，我们也看到类似情况，既体现在发起人（promoter）文化上，也体现在印度的国有企业上。所以总的来说，这正是我们真正试图加以利用的地方。如果你从整体来看新兴市场，指数中按市值计算大约有四分之一的公司是国有企业。所以整体上我们尽量远离它们，除非我们发现有这样一种情况：政府被逼到墙角，资产负债表被过度膨胀，需要一个扭转局面的故事，而政府选择退到一边说：“好吧，我们要引入私人管理层。我们会允许他们缩减资产负债表、出售非核心资产、设定真正与少数股东利益一致、有意义的KPI，从而把投资者重新吸引到这类公司中来。”所以有时候，它们反而能成就你能找到的最好的一些困境反转故事。但从整体上讲，这是你必须非常谨慎对待的东西，而且它可能是宽基指数最大的缺陷之一。那么其实，我想反过来问一个问题：新兴市场里是否真的有任何一部分，是你认为主动管理相对于指数并没有太大优势的？还是说，无论你投资哪里，主动管理其实都是最好的方式？不，我认为无论你用哪种方式——主动也好被动也好——如今都有多种不同的方式来参与新兴市场。这可能是我们现在与20年前之间看到的最大差异之一。过去你只要进入新兴市场、买入指数，就会说：“好的，这给了我一些分散化，给了我一些通胀保护，还有一些对美元可能走弱的保护。”但新兴市场已经演变，而过去几十年里人们并没有像他们本应做的那样去深入了解其内部构成。如今你看到的是巨大的集中度风险。你会看到新兴市场指数中大约40%由硬件科技、半导体构成；大约20%配置到中国，近30%到台湾地区，相当大一部分到韩国，而整个亚洲合计占80%。所以如果你作为一名普通投资者退后一步说：“等一下，我以为我买到的是东欧的价值交易、东南亚的结构性增长机会，或者拉美的政治改革故事。”其实你并没有。你基本上只获得了极小的敞口。所以从投资者的角度，你可以通过被动策略来做，但你自己其实是在主动操作。你可以说：“我想主动构建自己的新兴市场敞口，我可以买被动的阿根廷、被动的哥伦比亚、被动的希腊、被动的越南等等”——这些国家有很多独特的、令人兴奋的增长驱动因素，当下正呈现很强的动能——而无需买入宽基被动指数。另一种方式，也就是说这是一种把“主动”理解为亲力亲为的思路：买入单个国家或地区特定的被动产品；或者从更宏观的角度说：“我没时间做这个。我没法研究所有这些国家，也不一定了解正在发生什么。我知道我想要新兴市场敞口，但我不喜欢这个基准的构建方式。”那你就去找一位主动管理人，基本上是把选股和国家配置外包给了他。我认为这是很多人更倾向于采用的方式，因为你可以设定好之后就不用再操心了。

turns.en: Okay, that makes sense. You know, one of the things when I do manager, Laura, look at manager performance, you know, emerging markets and other categories like small caps, you know, I always think that managers tend to perform better than large cap managers due to more of a, information advantage that, you know, say like U.S. large cap managers, you know, because everyone's kind of looking at the same thing. Do you think as more active gets into emerging markets, that information advantage can narrow as those markets develop?
turns.zh: 好的，这说得通。你知道，当我做基金经理研究、查看基金经理业绩时——比如新兴市场和小盘股等其他类别——我总觉得这些经理往往比大盘股经理表现更好，因为他们有更多的信息优势，而像美国大盘股经理那样，大家都在看同样的东西。你认为随着更多主动管理资金进入新兴市场，随着这些市场发展，那种信息优势会不会缩小？

turns.en: Well, there are plenty of active managers, and it kind of depends if you're looking at local managers or U.S. managers. And I think that's an area where GlobalX and Murray Asset has a bit of an advantage. is that, yes, GlobalX is headquartered in New York. We are a U.S. firm. When I'm looking at our local India strategy, we have 14 on-the-ground analysts in Mumbai. When we're speaking about our Global EM, our Global EM ex-China strategy, yes, we have various analysts in this hemisphere, but we've got eight on-the-ground analysts in Hong Kong. So being able to be closer to the information from a language perspective, from a company access perspective, from really knowing the products, actually using them, growing up with them, I think that provides a tremendous advantage. But big picture, compared to the U.S., considering most of the capital still comes from the United States, I think that information gap is a big inefficiency that people can take advantage of because that's here to stay because most investors are sitting in the U.S. and they're going to get to the story a little later than locals.
turns.zh: 嗯，主动管理人有很多，这在一定程度上取决于你看的是本地管理人还是美国管理人。我认为这正是Global X和Mirae Asset（未来资产）略有优势的领域。是的，Global X总部位于纽约，我们是一家美国公司。但当我看我们的印度本地策略时，我们在孟买有14名驻地分析师。谈到我们的全球新兴市场、全球不含中国新兴市场策略时，是的，我们在本半球有若干分析师，但我们在香港有8名驻地分析师。所以能够从语言角度、从接触公司的角度更贴近信息，真正了解这些产品、实际使用它们、与它们一起成长，我认为这带来了巨大的优势。但从大局看，与美国相比，考虑到大部分资本仍然来自美国，我认为这种信息差距是一个人们可以利用的巨大市场低效，因为它会长期存在——大多数投资者都坐在美国，他们会比本地人稍晚一些才了解到这些故事。

turns.en: While we're still comparing investing in the U.S. versus emerging markets, You know, emerging market investing comes with risks that you and investors might not be familiar with. Currency, politics, different structure, market structures, name a few. But does that added complexity strengthen the case for active management?
turns.zh: 既然我们还在比较投资美国与投资新兴市场，你知道，新兴市场投资伴随着一些你和投资者可能不熟悉的风险——货币、政治、不同的市场结构等等，仅举几例。但这种额外的复杂性是否强化了主动管理的理由？

turns.en: I'd say so. I think complexity creates things an index can't really evaluate. Things that you mentioned, but also state ownership, which we discussed, related party dealing, something that we see often in India, currency and policy risk. An active manager can... can basically take advantage of opportunities and avoid risks. So EM's always going to be kind of moving. And one of the most important parts of performance is staying away from landmines. You can easily run a screen from a numeric perspective and say, this company looks cheap in emerging markets and growth looks good. And I think they seem to have a pretty good brand. But if you don't have someone who's sort of also paying attention saying, yes, but that country company also sits in a country where you have a huge fiscal deficit, a growing current account deficit, a central bank with no autonomy, inflation spiraling, and I don't know, you have an opaque political situation coming up with an election next year. You could be sitting in front of a truck in the form of a 40, 50% currency devaluation, and it doesn't matter how well that stock screened in the first place. And I think that's why a lot of kind of US or investors who kind of call themselves global sometimes have trouble when they become tourists and say, all right, I'm going to get some extra spice and buy a bank in Colombia or in Brazil or somewhere else because they're not doing that additional amount of diligence that active emerging market managers are doing day in and day out.
turns.zh: 我认为是的。我觉得复杂性会带来一些指数根本无法评估的东西——你提到的那些，还有我们讨论过的国有持股、关联交易（这在印度我们经常看到）、货币和政策风险。主动管理人基本上……能够利用机会并规避风险。新兴市场总是在变动，而业绩最重要的部分之一就是远离“地雷”。你很容易从数字角度跑一遍筛选，然后说：“这家公司在新兴市场里看起来很便宜，增长也不错，而且我觉得它的品牌似乎相当好。”但如果没有人同时在关注并指出：“是的，但那家公司所在的国家有巨额财政赤字、不断扩大的经常账户赤字、一个没有独立性的央行、失控飙升的通胀，而且——不好说——明年还有一场选举，政治局势扑朔迷离。”那你可能就正坐在一辆卡车面前，也就是40%、50%的货币贬值，这时那只股票当初筛选得多好都无所谓了。我认为这就是为什么很多自称全球化的美国投资者，有时会在他们变成“游客”时遇到麻烦——他们说：“好吧，我要来点额外的刺激，去哥伦比亚、巴西或其他地方买一家银行。”因为他们没有做主动型新兴市场管理人日复一日在做的那些额外的尽职调查。

turns.en: How often does liquidity become an issue?
turns.zh: 流动性多久会成为一个问题？

turns.en: You might find companies you like, but they're just not as liquid.
turns.zh: 你可能会找到自己喜欢的公司，但它们的流动性就是没那么好。

turns.en: Obviously, compared to the U.S., a lot of companies aren't going to be as liquid, but does liquidity ever become an issue for you?
turns.zh: 显然，与美国相比，很多公司的流动性都不会那么好，但流动性对你来说是否真的会成为问题？

turns.en: Yeah, it depends on the fund. Larger funds, you have to kind of be a little bit more cautious of small caps. And smaller funds, you can navigate them a lot more easily. But in deep markets like India and Brazil, we can build meaningful positions in mid-caps without moving prices. In some more shallow markets, a few liquid stocks limit what we can do from an active perspective. And the index already holds most of the opportunity set. So we size our positions to underlying liquidity, and that's a big part of our screening process as well.
turns.zh: 是的，这取决于基金。较大的基金，你对小盘股必须更谨慎一些；而较小的基金，你可以轻松得多地应对。但在像印度和巴西这样的深度市场，我们可以在中盘股中建立有意义的仓位而不推动价格。在一些更浅的市场，少数几只流动性好的股票限制了我们从主动角度能做的事情，而且指数已经持有了大部分机会集。所以我们会根据标的的流动性来确定仓位规模，这也是我们筛选流程中很重要的一部分。

turns.en: I want to go back to the index question as well. Obviously, the index is going to hold companies that I'm sure a lot of active managers don't think are quality companies, but do you think the index or the emerging markets benchmarks might actually be missing companies that are worth looking at? They are and they have in the past.
turns.zh: 我还想回到指数这个问题。显然，指数会持有一些我确信很多主动管理人并不认为是优质公司的股票，但你认为指数或新兴市场基准是否可能实际上遗漏了一些值得关注的公司？它们确实会遗漏，而且过去也一直如此。

turns.en: It took forever for companies like JD.com and Baba and Tencent, even NewBank more recently to get into the index. Indexes are generally backwards looking and it takes a meaningful amount of time for companies to be listed and then come up for consideration and go through various different processes before they're added to the passive benchmarks. So capital market access from an active perspective can be really meaningful. If you look at a company, the Chinese semiconductor company CXMT that went public a few months ago, it was up 500% in the first day. That still hasn't made it to the main benchmarks. So there are really meaningful opportunities like that. And then in addition to that, the way that a lot of benchmarks are set up, they're looking at local exchanges. But this day and age, like, No, the largest McDonald's franchisor in Latin America trades in the U.S., and it's not going to be part of any index. The largest e-commerce company in Latin America, MercadoLibre, trades in the U.S., not a part of any index. From a commodity perspective, which is a really meaningful part of many parts of emerging markets, companies tend to list in Canada because there's a capital market system that's very comfortable with mining companies. All their assets might be in Latin America or in Africa, but they're listed in Canada, so they're not going to be included in these passive indexes. And some of these companies, because they're listing in the US or Canada or London, they have higher standards of governance and they more often than not, they're on the higher end of the quality spectrum. And the fact that they're being left out of those indexes, I think, is a detriment for investors looking for EM exposure.
turns.zh: 像京东、阿里巴巴、腾讯，乃至最近的Nubank这样的公司，都花了极长时间才被纳入指数。指数通常是向后看的，一家公司要上市、然后进入考虑范围、再经历各种不同的流程，才会被加入被动基准，这需要相当长的时间。所以从主动角度来看，对资本市场的接触可能真的很有意义。如果你看一家公司——几个月前上市的中国半导体公司长鑫存储（CXMT），首日就上涨了500%，但它至今仍未进入主要基准。所以确实存在这样非常有意义的机会。此外，很多基准的构建方式是看本地交易所。但在当今时代，比如——不，拉美最大的麦当劳特许经营商在美国交易，它不会成为任何指数的一部分；拉美最大的电商公司MercadoLibre（美客多）在美国交易，也不属于任何指数。从大宗商品角度来看——这是新兴市场很多地区非常重要的组成部分——这些公司往往在加拿大上市，因为那里的资本市场体系对矿业公司非常熟悉。它们的全部资产可能在拉美或非洲，但由于在加拿大上市，就不会被纳入这些被动指数。而且其中一些公司，正是因为在美国、加拿大或伦敦上市，拥有更高的治理标准，往往处于质量光谱的较高端。它们被这些指数排除在外，我认为对那些寻求新兴市场敞口的投资者来说是一种损害。

turns.en: Could you walk us through why investors may prefer targeted country or regional allocations over broad emerging markets exposure?
turns.zh: 你能给我们讲讲，为什么投资者可能更偏好有针对性的国家或地区配置，而不是宽基的新兴市场敞口吗？

turns.en: Sure. I mean, targeted allocations let investors choose the size of each bet and own a Colombia and India or Brazil for specific reasons. So right now, we're seeing a lot of attention towards these Latin American countries like Argentina, Colombia, and Brazil for a combination of wanting exposure to commodities in this sort of high commodity environment that we're living in for powerful carry trades and for political reform. Most recently, we saw India go through a fantastic wave of performance that ended up selling off over the past two years for two reasons. One, because they faced a difficult tariff situation, and second, because energy prices spiked over the past year because of the conflict in Iran. But now a lot of tactical investors are saying, all right, I don't think this situation is sustainable in Iran. I think we'll see normalization. And in the meantime, OPEC has fallen apart. We're seeing more production come online. I think we'll see more supply come from Venezuela. I've got a call that oil could be at $ 50, $ 60 a barrel. And how can I take advantage of that besides simply shorting oil? They're looking for importers. They're looking for beneficiaries. And that's why a lot of people are starting to do work in countries like India or in Southeast Asia, because they think that if I have this targeted approach, I'm going to find an upside when their thesis plays out. Awesome.
turns.zh: 当然。有针对性的配置让投资者能够选择每一笔下注的规模，并出于特定理由持有哥伦比亚、印度或巴西。所以现在，我们看到大量关注投向这些拉美国家，比如阿根廷、哥伦比亚和巴西，原因有几个方面：一是想在我们所处的这种高大宗商品价格环境中获得大宗商品敞口，二是有力的套利交易（carry trade），三是政治改革。最近，我们看到印度经历了一波精彩的行情，但过去两年最终却出现抛售，原因有两个：一是它们面临棘手的关税局面，二是过去一年由于伊朗冲突导致能源价格飙升。但现在很多战术型投资者在说：“好吧，我不认为伊朗的这种局势会持续下去，我认为我们会看到局势正常化。与此同时，OPEC已经瓦解，我们看到更多产能投产，我认为会看到更多来自委内瑞拉的供应。我有个判断，油价可能跌到每桶50、60美元。那么除了简单做空石油，我该如何从中获利？”他们在寻找进口方，寻找受益者。这就是为什么很多人开始研究印度或东南亚等国家，因为他们认为，如果采用这种有针对性的方法，当自己的投资逻辑兑现时，就能找到上行空间。太好了。

turns.en: So we've discussed some shortcomings of broad benchmarks, including concentration. But how is it that active management can help address those concerns?
turns.zh: 我们已经讨论了宽基基准的一些缺陷，包括集中度。那么主动管理如何帮助应对这些问题呢？

turns.en: Well, in terms of addressing those flaws, there are a few different ways to do so. First of all, from a concentration perspective, are you getting concentration because this is the largest, most liquid company, which if you attach that to historical standards, that might be because it was a state-owned enterprise and had a lot of government and state support, despite not actually being the most profitable or accretive focused type of company? Or are you getting concentration that you do in some active funds because these are high conviction picks? So it's important to kind of balance that. What type of concentration are you getting? I think also within an active strategy, you do have opportunities for more diversification, more trends towards and focus on risk management, making sure you don't have position sizes above a certain level, country sizes above a certain level, sector sizes above a certain level. and making sure you're getting that full broad exposure to all the really good and attractive stories in a bigger picture emerging markets perspective. In addition to that, you can find managers that are focused on staying away from state-owned enterprises, managers that are focused on value or managers that are focused on growth, and really managers that are looking to partner with the end investor to be good stewards of capital over a long period of time.
turns.zh: 嗯，在应对这些缺陷方面，有几种不同的方法。首先，从集中度的角度看，你之所以集中，是因为这是最大、流动性最好的公司吗？如果结合历史标准来看，那可能是因为它曾是一家国有企业，得到了大量政府和国家支持，尽管它实际上并不是最盈利或最注重增值效应的那类公司？还是说，你像某些主动型基金那样集中，是因为这些是高信念的选股？所以权衡这一点很重要：你获得的是哪种类型的集中度？我认为，在主动策略中，你确实有机会实现更多分散化，更加注重并聚焦于风险管理，确保你的仓位规模、国家规模、行业规模都不超过某个水平，并确保你从更宏观的新兴市场角度获得对那些真正优秀、有吸引力的故事的全面广泛敞口。此外，你还可以找到那些专注于远离国有企业的管理人、专注于价值的管理人或专注于成长的管理人，以及真正希望与最终投资者结成伙伴、在长期内做优秀资本管家的管理人。

turns.en: So it's clear concentration seems to cut both ways in emerging markets. you know, broad market indices can be heavily concentrated in certain countries or companies, but active managers also have the flexibility to concentrate in their highest conviction ideas. How do you think about that trade-off?
turns.zh: 所以很显然，集中度在新兴市场似乎是一把双刃剑。宽基市场指数可能高度集中于某些国家或公司，但主动管理人也有灵活度，把仓位集中在他们信念最高的想法上。你如何看待这种权衡？

turns.en: Yeah, I mean, they differ in kind. It's a great point. And benchmark concentration comes from price momentum. The weights rise because stocks rose. Did they rise because of fundamental reasons or was it a momentum, a swinging momentum? And is it sustainable? Because you don't want to chase something that's gone up a lot and then kind of be in the wrong place at the wrong time. Conviction, on the other hand, conviction can lead to concentration coming from work, from bottom up fundamental analysis, where you actually believe that there are bright prospects for the future. So we own fewer names because we know why we own them and we really like them. And we think that these are compounding machines for a four to five year period. We don't just own them because they've done well over the past six months. So my next question might be more towards your specific philosophy, but you mentioned a bottom-up. When you're actually investing and building a portfolio, do your decisions focus completely on bottom-up and let your security selection drive the country allocations in the portfolio, or do you ever kind of do top-down, picking a country first and then kind of digging in to see what's going on in that country? I'd say the bottom up tends, it's really a blend. I think a lot of managers will come out and say, oh, we have a strict framework. We just are bottom up fundamental investors. We don't focus on the macro at all. And we certainly are. We do our diligence and we are very much in the weeds with these companies, you know, visiting companies. headquarters and manufacturing centers and distribution outlets and all of that and running so many sensitivity analyses on our models. But that's the key thing. What are the inputs into your model at the end of the day? Interest rates are going to have a huge impact on the asset quality of banks or the net interest margins of banks or your net interest expenses of the debt you have on a different type of company. Currency is going to have a strong impact on The cost of goods sold, if you're importing inputs from other countries, it's also going to have an impact on your revenues if you're selling to different countries. So you have to have an understanding of the macro to get to the fundamental bottom-up analysis properly. If not, I think you're kind of doing yourself a disservice.
turns.zh: 是的，它们的性质不同。这是个很好的观点。基准的集中度来自价格动量：权重上升是因为股价上涨了。它们上涨是因为基本面原因，还是因为一种摆动的动量？这种上涨可持续吗？因为你不会想去追逐一个已经涨了很多的东西，然后在错误的时间出现在错误的地方。另一方面，信念——信念可以带来集中度，而这种集中度来自扎实的工作、来自自下而上的基本面分析，你真正相信未来有光明的前景。所以我们持有较少的股票，是因为我们知道为什么持有它们、我们真的很喜欢它们，我们认为这些是能在四到五年期间持续复利的机器。我们持有它们，并不只是因为它们在过去六个月表现良好。那么我的下一个问题可能更偏向你的具体投资理念。你提到了自下而上。当你实际投资和构建投资组合时，你的决策是完全聚焦于自下而上、让选股来驱动组合中的国家配置，还是你有时也会做自上而下——先选定一个国家，然后再深入去看那个国家正在发生什么？我会说，自下而上其实是一种混合。我认为很多管理人会站出来说：“哦，我们有一套严格的框架。我们就是自下而上的基本面投资者，完全不关注宏观。”而我们当然也是自下而上的：我们做尽职调查，深入到这些公司的细节之中，比如拜访公司总部、制造中心和分销网点等等，并在我们的模型上做大量的敏感性分析。但关键在于：说到底，你模型的输入项是什么？利率会对银行的资产质量、银行的净息差，或另一类公司所背负债务的净利息支出产生巨大影响。汇率会强烈影响销货成本——如果你从其他国家进口投入品的话；如果你向不同国家销售，它也会影响你的收入。所以你必须对宏观有理解，才能正确地做好自下而上的基本面分析。否则，我认为你其实是在坑自己。

turns.en: Yeah, no, definitely makes sense. And we all know China dominated the benchmarks for a while. And I know a couple of years ago, there was kind of an influx of these ex-China emerging markets products. And I'm just curious, with China still a pretty big allocation, especially in the benchmarks and even to a lot of funds to that extent, do you think that's caused investors to overlook other opportunities just because China was such a big part of the conversation for so long?
turns.zh: 是的，绝对说得通。我们都知道中国一度主导了这些基准。我也知道几年前涌现了一批不含中国的新兴市场产品。我只是好奇，鉴于中国仍然是相当大的一块配置——尤其是在基准中，甚至对很多基金来说也是如此——你认为这是否导致投资者忽视了其他机会，只因为中国在这么长时间里都是话题中如此重要的一部分？

turns.en: So is the question... Did China lead investors to overlook opportunities in the past, or are people overlooking China now because ex-China has become such a meaningful opportunity?
turns.zh: 所以你的问题是……过去是中国导致投资者忽视了其他机会，还是现在人们正在忽视中国，因为“不含中国”已经变成了一个如此有意义的机会？

turns.en: Well, I think it's, are people still, are they still kind of overlooking other things still now?
turns.zh: 嗯，我想问的是，人们现在是否仍然在忽视其他东西？

turns.en: I think they're overlooking a big part of emerging markets, not so much because of China anymore, because as you mentioned, with the evolution of ex-China products such as our own, you have the opportunity to be in emerging markets without direct China exposure. Or you could buy an ex-China product and say, I want some China exposure, but I only want exposure to China consumer discretionary. So then you buy a different ETF and size up your China opportunity in a more targeted manner in the way that you want it to create a complete broad EM portfolio. So I would like blame China as a whole anymore because you have opportunities to strip it out and size it. But I do think big parts of emerging markets are getting overlooked because of the concentration risk in other places. So we mentioned semiconductors, we mentioned Korea, we mentioned Taiwan, but not just like three companies from a company specific basis. SK Hynix, Samsung and TSMC, they represent over 30% of the broad emerging market index as a whole. Just three companies. And that's really remarkable because they are taking weight not only from other companies, but other countries as a whole. And if you look at a country like Colombia, one of the best performing countries this year, dynamic political change just this past June, you know, less low single digit exposure. Similar for Greece. Greece is up 112 percent over the past two years. Most people own none of it because it represents roughly one to two percent exposure of the emerging markets index. So, yeah, there are a lot of really great dynamic stories that have been performing that should continue to perform. But if you buy the broad index, you're not getting enough of exposure. And if you're doing it yourself, you might not be getting any exposure either just because you're not aware of these situations because they're not getting the headlines within the benchmark. When it comes to.
turns.zh: 我认为他们正在忽视新兴市场的很大一部分，而这已不再主要是因为中国，因为正如你提到的，随着“不含中国”产品（比如我们自己的产品）的发展，你有机会参与新兴市场而没有直接的中国敞口。或者你可以买一个不含中国的产品，然后说：“我想要一些中国敞口，但只想要中国非必需消费品的敞口。”于是你再买另一只ETF，以更有针对性的方式、按你想要的方式来配置你的中国机会，从而构建一个完整的宽基新兴市场组合。所以我不再想把责任整个归咎于中国，因为你有机会把它剔除、并按需配置它。但我确实认为，新兴市场很大一部分正被忽视，原因在于其他地方的集中度风险。我们提到了半导体，提到了韩国、提到了台湾地区，但不仅是这些——单从公司层面看，仅仅三家公司：SK海力士、三星和台积电，它们合计就占了整个宽基新兴市场指数的30%以上。仅仅三家公司。这真的很不寻常，因为它们不仅在从其他公司那里夺取权重，而且在从整个其他国家那里夺取权重。如果你看哥伦比亚这样的国家——它是今年表现最好的国家之一，就在今年6月经历了充满活力的政治变革——你会发现它在指数中的敞口不到低个位数。希腊也类似。希腊在过去两年上涨了112%。大多数人一点都没持有，因为它在新兴市场指数中只占大约1%到2%的敞口。所以，是的，有很多非常棒的、充满活力的故事一直在表现出色，而且应该会继续表现出色。但如果你买宽基指数，你获得的敞口并不够。而如果你亲力亲为，你可能也得不到任何敞口，仅仅是因为你没有意识到这些情况——因为它们没有在基准中占据头条。当谈到……

turns.en: Different countries, GlobalX has been enthusiastic about markets like India or Brazil. What characteristics make a market attractive to you, emerging or otherwise?
turns.zh: 说到不同的国家，Global X一直对印度或巴西这样的市场充满热情。什么样的特质会让一个市场——无论是否是新兴市场——对你有吸引力？

turns.en: Yeah, I mean, first of all, I think two questions is, you know, when we're deciding to launch a passive product or an active product. And when we're looking to launch an active product, we're only doing so where we find inefficient markets. So we think that India and Brazil and broad emerging markets and broad EMX China are are deep enough, liquid enough, and inefficient enough where our expert management teams can take advantage of those inefficiencies and add value. But in terms of what characteristics more broadly make markets attractive to us, I mean, India checks so many boxes. I think it's the best structural opportunity in international markets. It's the best demographic dividend potentially in the world. youngest population in the world largest youth population in the world largest population in the world largest youth population in the world very educated youth population. You also have a very market-friendly government focused on fiscal consolidation, digitalization, and broad market-friendly reforms. You have a consumer class that's really hitting its inflection point in terms of discretionary spending. And you have a lot of foreign direct investment coming into the country. So if you look at what drives GDP, it's net exports plus private investment plus government spending plus consumer spending. That's what makes up GDP growth. And so we're looking for countries that can check as many of those variables as possible. India checks all of them. Brazil does a lot on the consumer side. probably does a little too much in terms of government spending, but it's doing very well in terms of net exports more recently because of this commodity boom. We see a lot of opportunities in other countries as well, including Argentina, Vietnam, and Colombia. It's fascinating.
turns.zh: 是的，首先，我认为有两个问题——就是在决定推出一只被动产品还是主动产品时。而当我们考虑推出主动产品时，我们只会在我们发现市场低效的地方去做。所以我们认为，印度、巴西以及宽基新兴市场和宽基不含中国新兴市场，都足够深、流动性足够好、也足够低效，我们专业的管理团队能够利用这些低效并创造价值。但就更宏观地说什么样的特质让市场对我们有吸引力而言——印度满足了非常多的条件。我认为它是国际市场中最好的结构性机会，可能是世界上最好的人口红利。它拥有世界上最年轻的人口、世界上最大的青年人口、世界上最大的人口，以及受教育程度很高的青年人口。你还有一个非常亲市场的政府，专注于财政整固、数字化和广泛的亲市场改革。你有一个消费群体，在非必需品支出方面正真正到达拐点。而且有大量外国直接投资流入该国。所以如果你看是什么驱动GDP，那就是净出口加私人投资加政府支出加消费支出，这些构成了GDP增长。因此我们寻找的是能够尽可能满足这些变量中越多越好的国家。印度全部满足。巴西在消费方面做得很多，可能在政府支出方面做得有点过头，但最近由于大宗商品繁荣，它在净出口方面表现得非常好。我们也在其他国家看到很多机会，包括阿根廷、越南和哥伦比亚。这非常迷人。

turns.en: So you've mentioned alignment with minority shareholders a few times through this. Why is that particularly important for emerging markets? And what does that tell us about how active managers could have an advantage?
turns.zh: 你在整个对话中几次提到与少数股东利益保持一致。为什么这一点对新兴市场尤其重要？它又能告诉我们主动管理人如何可能具备优势？

turns.en: Sure. Well, I guess in, in EM, the people in control often include the state or a founding family and, and their interests can differ from a minority shareholders. Um, you know, state owned banks, energy and utilities carry a lot of weight in, in broad EM and in Brazil and India specifically. Um, in India, promoters can compound capital alongside minorities for decades, or they can be, being on related party transactions, pledged shares, and kind of intertwined tangled group structures, which could leave minorities out in the dust. So I think alignment shows up in the cash flows that you actually receive. And when structuring an index, more often than not, they can't ask whether the people in control get paid only when minorities get paid. And that's where active research can add real value. Okay. Just have one more question before we let you go.
turns.zh: 当然。嗯，我想在新兴市场，掌控公司的人往往包括国家或创始家族，而他们的利益可能与少数股东不同。你知道，国有银行、能源和公用事业公司在宽基新兴市场中，尤其是在巴西和印度，占据很大权重。在印度，发起人（promoter）可以与少数股东并肩几十年让资本复利增长；但他们也可能搞关联交易、股权质押，以及那种相互交织、盘根错节的集团结构，这些可能把少数股东远远甩在后面。所以我认为，利益一致性体现在你实际收到的现金流上。而在构建指数时，它们往往无法去追问：掌控公司的人是否只有在少数股东拿到回报时才能得到回报。而这正是主动研究能够创造真正价值的地方。好的。在放你走之前，我们还有一个问题。

turns.en: Obviously, we track what's happening with product launches and where flows are going in assets. Active ETFs have obviously grown pretty rapidly in the U.S., or I should say particularly in domestic strategies. What do you think has to happen for active emerging market ETFs to gain broader adoption?
turns.zh: 显然，我们会追踪产品发行的动态以及资产流向何处。主动型ETF在美国增长得相当迅速——或者我应该说，尤其是在国内（美国本土）策略中。你认为主动型新兴市场ETF要获得更广泛的采用，需要发生什么？

turns.en: Flows just have to come back to the asset class. And it probably flows when they do come back, as we've been seeing over the past couple of years. It's first going to be performance driven. And after you see that strong outperformance, it tends to move into passive first. And then when people actually build up conviction that they want this to be a core part of their asset allocation, that's when they kind of look under the hood, do more diligence and do it from a more sophisticated approach and say, I need an actual steward of capital that's going to protect me through volatility, smooth out my performance and make sure that our sort of KPIs are aligned. So it comes from outperformance, inefficiencies built up by flows chasing that performance, and then active being able to step in and outperform.
turns.zh: 资金流必须重新回到这个资产类别。而当资金确实回流时——正如我们过去几年所看到的——它首先会由业绩驱动。在你看到那种强劲的超额表现之后，资金往往会先流入被动产品。然后，当人们真正建立起信念、希望它成为自己资产配置的核心部分时，他们才会去深入了解内部构成、做更多尽职调查，并以更成熟的方式来操作，然后说：“我需要一个真正的资本管家，能在波动中保护我、平滑我的业绩，并确保我们的KPI是一致的。”所以这来自超额表现、来自资金追逐这种表现所累积出的低效，然后主动管理得以介入并跑赢。

turns.en: It'll be something to watch, but definitely looking forward to it. But we need to end here. But this was a lot of fun, Malcolm. Thanks again for joining us. Great being with you guys. Thanks so much. And True, I also want to thank you for being my co-host today.
turns.zh: 这将是值得关注的事情，我也肯定很期待。不过我们得在这里结束了。这非常有趣，Malcolm，再次感谢你加入我们。“和你们在一起很棒，非常感谢。”另外Sharun，我也要感谢你今天担任我的联合主持人。

turns.en: Thanks, David. Thanks, Malcolm.
turns.zh: 谢谢你，David。谢谢你，Malcolm。

turns.en: And I also want to thank our listeners. If you liked the episode, please share it, subscribe, and leave a review. And if you'd like to see more of our research on the Terminal, Go to BIFundGo for U.S. fund and active research. Until our next episode, this is David Cohn with Inside Active.
turns.zh: 我还要感谢我们的听众。如果你喜欢这一期节目，请分享、订阅并留下评价。如果你想在彭博终端（Terminal）上查看更多我们的研究，请输入BIFundGo，获取美国基金和主动管理研究。下期节目再见，我是《Inside Active》的David Cohne。
